In the survey, what is the exact number of Latinos who report They expect their financial
situation as well as their family’s
to be better a year from now and belong to the group Live in a household with
job or wage loss during
the pandemic? Round the answer down to the nearest integer.

paragraphs.text: More than a year into the pandemic, Latinos in the United States say COVID19 has harmed them and their loved ones in many ways. About half say a family member or close friend has been hospitalized or died from the coronavirus, and a similar share say they or someone in their household has lost a job or taken a pay cut during the pandemic. Yet amid these hardships, Latinos are upbeat about the future. Nearly twothirds say the worst of the coronavirus outbreak is behind the country, and a majority say they expect their financial situation and that of their family to improve over the next year.

Job and wage losses in Latino households during the pandemic were just as likely for those born in another country as those born in the U.S., according to a bilingual, online survey of 3,375 U.S. Latino adults conducted in March 2021. However, among immigrant Latinos, some groups were harder hit than others – a relatively high share (58%) of Latino immigrants without U.S. citizenship and without a green card say they or someone in their household has lost a job or wages since February 2020, compared with 45% of naturalized U.S. citizen immigrants who say this.1

Yet Latinos see better days ahead for themselves and the country, even if they have experienced hardship due to COVID-19. Most Latinos say they think the worst of the problems the country is facing from the outbreak are behind us, with similar majorities saying so among those who have had and not had someone close to them hospitalized or die due to the coronavirus. In addition, a slight majority of Latinos (54%) say they expect their personal financial situation will be better a year from now, with only modest differences between those in households that have and have not experienced a loss of jobs or wages since the start of the pandemic.
Terminology
The terms Hispanic and Latino are used interchangeably in this report.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term U.S. born refers to people who are U.S. citizens at birth, including people born in the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories, as well as those born elsewhere to at least one parent who is a U.S. citizen.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term foreign born refers to persons born outside of the United States to parents neither of whom was a U.S. citizen. The terms foreign born and immigrant are used interchangeably in this report.
Second generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with at least one first-generation, or immigrant, parent.

Third or higher generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with both parents born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories.

Over the course of the pandemic, Latinos have become more optimistic about the country. About half (49%) say they are satisfied with the nation’s direction, up from June 2020, when 20% said the same. This is the most satisfied Latinos have been with the nation’s direction since 2012, when 51% said so. At the same time, the share saying the worst of the pandemic is behind us as a nation is up sharply, from 23% in April 2020 to 65% in March 2021. Meanwhile, Latino adults are more likely today than before the pandemic to say the situation of U.S. Latinos has improved or stayed about the same over the past year, and they are less likely to say the situation of Latinos has worsened.

在调查中，表示他们预计一年后自己

会有所改善且属于所在家庭在疫情期间
有人失业
或工资减少群体的拉丁裔确切人数是多少？将答案向下取整到最接近的整数。

paragraphs.text: 疫情暴发一年多以来，美国拉丁裔表示，COVID19在许多方面伤害了他们及其亲友。约一半的人表示，有家人或密友因感染冠状病毒而住院或去世，另有相近比例的人表示，他们本人或家中有人在疫情期间失业或被减薪。然而，尽管面临这些困难，拉丁裔仍对未来持乐观态度。近三分之二的人表示，美国已经度过了冠状病毒疫情最严重的阶段，多数人表示，他们预计自己及家人的财务状况将在未来一年有所改善。

根据2021年三月对3,375名美国拉丁裔成年人开展的一项双语在线调查，在疫情期间，出生于其他国家的拉丁裔家庭与出生于美国的拉丁裔家庭遭遇失业和工资损失的可能性相同。然而，在拉丁裔移民中，一些群体受到的冲击比其他群体更大：既没有美国公民身份也没有绿卡的拉丁裔移民中，表示自2020年二月以来自己或家中有人失业或遭遇工资损失的比例相对较高，为58%；相比之下，已归化为美国公民的移民中，这一比例为45%。1
然而，即便因COVID-19经历了困难，拉丁裔仍认为自己和国家将迎来更好的日子。大多数拉丁裔表示，他们认为国家因疫情暴发而面临的最严重问题已经过去；无论是否有亲近的人因感染冠状病毒而住院或去世，持这一看法的人都占多数，且比例相近。此外，略多于半数的拉丁裔（54%）表示，他们预计一年后个人财务状况会有所改善；自疫情开始以来家庭经历过失业或工资损失的人与未经历过这些情况的人之间，仅存在不大的差异。
术语
本报告中，西班牙裔与拉丁裔两个术语可互换使用。
除非另有说明，“美国出生”一词指生来即为美国公民的人，包括出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土的人，以及出生于其他地方但父母中至少一方为美国公民的人。
除非另有说明，“外国出生”一词指出生于美国境外且父母双方均非美国公民的人。本报告中，“外国出生”与“移民”两个术语可互换使用。
第二代指出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土，且父母中至少一方为第一代移民的人。
第三代或更高世代指出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土，且父母双方均出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土的人。

在疫情期间，拉丁裔对国家变得更加乐观。约一半（49%）表示，他们对国家的发展方向感到满意，高于2020年六月的20%。这是自2012年以来拉丁裔对国家发展方向最满意的一次，当时有51%的人表示满意。与此同时，认为全国已经度过疫情最严重阶段的人所占比例大幅上升，从2020年四月的23%升至2021年三月的65%。此外，与疫情前相比，如今拉丁裔成年人更有可能表示，美国拉丁裔的处境在过去一年有所改善或基本保持不变，而表示拉丁裔处境恶化的可能性则有所降低。

paragraphs.text: More than a year into the pandemic, Latinos in the United States say COVID19 has harmed them and their loved ones in many ways. About half say a family member or close friend has been hospitalized or died from the coronavirus, and a similar share say they or someone in their household has lost a job or taken a pay cut during the pandemic. Yet amid these hardships, Latinos are upbeat about the future. Job and wage losses in Latino households during the pandemic were just as likely for those born in another country as those born in the U.S., according to a bilingual, online survey of 3,375 U.S. Latino adults conducted in March 2021. However, among immigrant Latinos, some groups were harder hit than others – a relatively high share (58%) of Latino immigrants without U.S. citizenship and without a green card say they or someone in their household has lost a job or wages since February 2020, compared with 45% of naturalized U.S. citizen immigrants who say this.1

Yet Latinos see better days ahead for themselves and the country, even if they have experienced hardship due to COVID-19. Most Latinos say they think the worst of the problems the country is facing from the outbreak are behind us, with similar majorities saying so among those who have had and not had someone close to them hospitalized or die due to the coronavirus. In addition, a slight majority of Latinos (54%) say they expect their personal financial situation will be better a year from now, with only modest differences between those in households that have and have not experienced a loss of jobs or wages since the start of the pandemic.
Terminology
The terms Hispanic and Latino are used interchangeably in this report.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term U.S. born refers to people who are U.S. citizens at birth, including people born in the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories, as well as those born elsewhere to at least one parent who is a U.S. citizen.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term foreign born refers to persons born outside of the United States to parents neither of whom was a U.S. citizen. The terms foreign born and immigrant are used interchangeably in this report.
Second generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with at least one first-generation, or immigrant, parent.

Third or higher generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with both parents born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories.

Over the course of the pandemic, Latinos have become more optimistic about the country. About half (49%) say they are satisfied with the nation’s direction, up from June 2020, when 20% said the same. This is the most satisfied Latinos have been with the nation’s direction since 2012, when 51% said so. At the same time, the share saying the worst of the pandemic is behind us as a nation is up sharply, from 23% in April 2020 to 65% in March 2021. Meanwhile, Latino adults are more likely today than before the pandemic to say the situation of U.S. Latinos has improved or stayed about the same over the past year, and they are less likely to say the situation of Latinos has worsened.

query:
この調査で、1年後には自分と家族の
経済状況が
改善すると予想していると回答し、パンデミック中に
失業や賃金減少のあった
世帯で暮らしているのグループに属するラティーノの正確な人数は何人ですか？小数点以下を切り捨てて整数で答えてください。

paragraphs.text: パンデミックの発生から一年以上が経過し、米国のラティーノは、COVID19が自分たちや大切な人々にさまざまな害を及ぼしたと述べている。約半数が、家族や親しい友人が新型コロナウイルスによって入院したり亡くなったりしたと答え、同程度の割合が、パンデミック中に自分自身または同じ世帯の誰かが失業したり給与を減らされたりしたと答えている。しかし、こうした困難の中でも、ラティーノは将来に対して楽観的だ。三分の二近くが、国内の新型コロナウイルス感染拡大は最悪の時期を過ぎたと答え、過半数が、今後一年間で自分自身と家族の経済状況が改善すると予想している。

2021年三月に米国のラティーノの成人3,375人を対象として二言語で実施されたオンライン調査によると、パンデミック中にラティーノの世帯が失業や賃金減少を経験する可能性は、外国生まれの人も米国生まれの人も同程度だった。しかし、移民のラティーノの中には、他の集団よりも大きな打撃を受けた集団もあった。米国市民権もグリーンカードも持たないラティーノ移民のうち、2020年二月以降に自分自身または同じ世帯の誰かが失業や賃金減少を経験したと答えた人の割合は比較的高く（58%）、帰化して米国市民となった移民では、その割合は45%だった。1

それでもラティーノは、COVID-19による困難を経験したとしても、自分たちと国の前途にはより良い日々が待っていると考えている。ラティーノの大半は、感染拡大によって国が直面している問題の最悪の時期は過ぎたと考えていると答えており、新型コロナウイルスによって身近な人が入院したり亡くなったりした経験がある人も、そうした経験がない人も、同程度の過半数がそのように答えている。さらに、ラティーノのわずかに過半数（54%）が、一年後には自分の経済状況が今より良くなると予想しており、パンデミックの発生以降に失業や賃金減少を経験した世帯の人と、経験していない世帯の人との差はわずかにとどまる。
用語
本報告書では、ヒスパニックとラティーノという用語を同じ意味で使用している。
特に断りのない限り、米国生まれという用語は、出生時に米国市民であった人を指す。これには、米国の50州、コロンビア特別区、プエルトリコ、その他の米国領で生まれた人に加え、少なくとも片方の親が米国市民で、その他の場所で生まれた人も含まれる。
特に断りのない限り、外国生まれという用語は、米国外で生まれ、両親のいずれも米国市民ではなかった人を指す。本報告書では、外国生まれと移民という用語を同じ意味で使用している。
第二世代とは、米国の50州、コロンビア特別区、プエルトリコ、その他の米国領で生まれ、少なくとも片方の親が第一世代、すなわち移民である人を指す。
第三世代以降とは、米国の50州、コロンビア特別区、プエルトリコ、その他の米国領で生まれ、両親ともに米国の50州、コロンビア特別区、プエルトリコ、その他の米国領で生まれた人を指す。

パンデミックが続く中、ラティーノは国の状況についてより楽観的になっている。約半数（49%）が国の進む方向に満足していると答えており、同じ回答が20%だった2020年六月から増加した。ラティーノが国の進む方向に満足している割合は、51%がそう答えた2012年以来、最も高い。同時に、国としてパンデミックの最悪の時期は過ぎたと答えた人の割合は、2020年四月の23%から2021年三月の65%へと急増している。一方、ラティーノの成人が、過去一年間に米国のラティーノの状況が改善した、またはほぼ変わらなかったと答える割合は、パンデミック前よりも現在のほうが高く、ラティーノの状況が悪化したと答える割合は低くなっている。

paragraphs.text: 팬데믹이 시작된 지 일 년이 넘은 시점에, 미국의 라틴계 주민들은 코로나19가 자신과 사랑하는 사람들에게 여러 면에서 피해를 주었다고 말한다. 약 절반은 가족이나 가까운 친구가 코로나바이러스로 입원하거나 사망했다고 답했으며, 비슷한 비율이 팬데믹 기간에 자신이나 가구 구성원이 일자리를 잃거나 임금이 삭감되었다고 답했다. 그러나 이러한 어려움 속에서도 라틴계 주민들은 미래를 낙관하고 있다. 거의 삼분의 이는 미국이 코로나바이러스 확산의 최악의 고비를 넘겼다고 말하며, 과반수는 향후 일 년 동안 자신과 가족의 재정 상황이 나아질 것으로 예상한다고 말한다.

2021년 삼월에 미국의 라틴계 성인 3,375명을 대상으로 두 언어로 실시한 온라인 설문조사에 따르면, 팬데믹 기간 라틴계 가구에서 발생한 실직과 임금 손실의 가능성은 다른 나라에서 태어난 사람들과 미국에서 태어난 사람들이 비슷했다. 그러나 라틴계 이민자 중에서는 일부 집단이 다른 집단보다 더 큰 타격을 입었다. 미국 시민권과 영주권이 모두 없는 라틴계 이민자 중 비교적 높은 비율(58%)이 2020년 이월 이후 자신이나 가구 구성원이 일자리를 잃거나 임금 손실을 겪었다고 답한 반면, 미국 시민권을 취득한 귀화 이민자 중에서는 45%가 그렇게 답했다.1

그러나 라틴계 주민들은 코로나-19로 어려움을 겪었더라도 자신과 국가에 더 나은 날들이 찾아올 것으로 보고 있다. 라틴계 주민 대다수는 코로나바이러스 확산으로 국가가 직면한 문제의 최악의 고비는 지났다고 생각한다고 답했으며, 가까운 사람이 코로나바이러스로 입원하거나 사망한 경험이 있는 사람들과 그렇지 않은 사람들 사이에서 비슷한 과반수가 그렇게 답했다. 또한 라틴계 주민의 절반을 조금 넘는 비율(54%)이 일 년 후 자신의 재정 상황이 더 나아질 것으로 예상한다고 답했으며, 팬데믹 시작 이후 실직이나 임금 손실을 경험한 가구에 속한 사람들과 그렇지 않은 가구에 속한 사람들 간의 차이는 크지 않았다.
용어
이 보고서에서는 히스패닉과 라틴계라는 용어를 같은 의미로 사용한다.
별도로 명시하지 않는 한, 미국 출생자라는 용어는 출생 시 미국 시민권을 가진 사람을 가리키며, 미국의 50개 주, 컬럼비아 특별구, 푸에르토리코 또는 기타 미국령에서 태어난 사람뿐 아니라 부모 중 적어도 한 명이 미국 시민인 사람으로서 그 밖의 지역에서 태어난 사람도 포함한다.
별도로 명시하지 않는 한, 외국 출생자라는 용어는 부모 모두 미국 시민이 아닌 사람으로서 미국 밖에서 태어난 사람을 가리킨다. 이 보고서에서는 외국 출생자와 이민자라는 용어를 같은 의미로 사용한다.
이 세대는 부모 중 적어도 한 명이 일 세대, 즉 이민자인 사람으로서 미국의 50개 주, 컬럼비아 특별구, 푸에르토리코 또는 기타 미국령에서 태어난 사람을 가리킨다.
삼 세대 이상은 부모 모두 미국의 50개 주, 컬럼비아 특별구, 푸에르토리코 또는 기타 미국령에서 태어난 사람으로서 자신도 미국의 50개 주, 컬럼비아 특별구, 푸에르토리코 또는 기타 미국령에서 태어난 사람을 가리킨다.

팬데믹을 거치면서 라틴계 주민들은 국가에 대해 더 낙관적으로 변했다. 약 절반(49%)은 국가가 나아가는 방향에 만족한다고 답했는데, 이는 2020년 유월에 같은 답변을 한 비율인 20%보다 높아진 것이다. 이는 2012년에 51%가 그렇게 답한 이후 라틴계 주민들이 국가가 나아가는 방향에 대해 보인 가장 높은 만족도다. 동시에 국가 차원에서 팬데믹의 최악의 고비가 지났다고 답한 비율은 2020년 사월의 23%에서 2021년 삼월의 65%로 급격히 상승했다. 한편 현재 라틴계 성인들은 팬데믹 이전보다 지난 일 년 동안 미국 라틴계 주민들의 상황이 개선되었거나 거의 그대로 유지되었다고 답할 가능성이 더 높으며, 라틴계 주민들의 상황이 악화되었다고 답할 가능성은 더 낮다.

query:
在调查中，表示他们预计一年后自己
及家人的财务状况
会有所改善且属于所在家庭在疫情期间
有人失业
或工资减少群体的拉丁裔确切人数是多少？将答案向下取整到最接近的整数。

paragraphs.text: 疫情暴发一年多以来，美国拉丁裔表示，COVID19在许多方面伤害了他们及其亲友。约一半的人表示，有家人或密友因感染冠状病毒而住院或去世，另有相近比例的人表示，他们本人或家中有人在疫情期间失业或被减薪。然而，尽管面临这些困难，拉丁裔仍对未来持乐观态度。近三分之二的人表示，美国已经度过了冠状病毒疫情最严重的阶段，多数人表示，他们预计自己及家人的财务状况将在未来一年有所改善。

根据2021年三月对3,375名美国拉丁裔成年人开展的一项双语在线调查，在疫情期间，出生于其他国家的拉丁裔家庭与出生于美国的拉丁裔家庭遭遇失业和工资损失的可能性相同。然而，在拉丁裔移民中，一些群体受到的冲击比其他群体更大：既没有美国公民身份也没有绿卡的拉丁裔移民中，表示自2020年二月以来自己或家中有人失业或遭遇工资损失的比例相对较高，为58%；相比之下，已归化为美国公民的移民中，这一比例为45%。1
然而，即便因COVID-19经历了困难，拉丁裔仍认为自己和国家将迎来更好的日子。大多数拉丁裔表示，他们认为国家因疫情暴发而面临的最严重问题已经过去；无论是否有亲近的人因感染冠状病毒而住院或去世，持这一看法的人都占多数，且比例相近。此外，略多于半数的拉丁裔（54%）表示，他们预计一年后个人财务状况会有所改善；自疫情开始以来家庭经历过失业或工资损失的人与未经历过这些情况的人之间，仅存在不大的差异。
术语
本报告中，西班牙裔与拉丁裔两个术语可互换使用。
除非另有说明，“美国出生”一词指生来即为美国公民的人，包括出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土的人，以及出生于其他地方但父母中至少一方为美国公民的人。
除非另有说明，“外国出生”一词指出生于美国境外且父母双方均非美国公民的人。本报告中，“外国出生”与“移民”两个术语可互换使用。
第二代指出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土，且父母中至少一方为第一代移民的人。
第三代或更高世代指出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土，且父母双方均出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土的人。

在疫情期间，拉丁裔对国家变得更加乐观。约一半（49%）表示，他们对国家的发展方向感到满意，高于2020年六月的20%。这是自2012年以来拉丁裔对国家发展方向最满意的一次，当时有51%的人表示满意。与此同时，认为全国已经度过疫情最严重阶段的人所占比例大幅上升，从2020年四月的23%升至2021年三月的65%。此外，与疫情前相比，如今拉丁裔成年人更有可能表示，美国拉丁裔的处境在过去一年有所改善或基本保持不变，而表示拉丁裔处境恶化的可能性则有所降低。

query:
In the survey, what is the exact number of Latinos who report They expect their financial
situation as well as their family’s
to be better a year from now and belong to the group Live in a household with
job or wage loss during
the pandemic? Round the answer down to the nearest integer.

paragraphs.text: More than a year into the pandemic, Latinos in the United States say COVID19 has harmed them and their loved ones in many ways. About half say a family member or close friend has been hospitalized or died from the coronavirus, and a similar share say they or someone in their household has lost a job or taken a pay cut during the pandemic. Yet amid these hardships, Latinos are upbeat about the future. Nearly twothirds say the worst of the coronavirus outbreak is behind the country, and a majority say they expect their financial situation and that of their family to improve over the next year.

Job and wage losses in Latino households during the pandemic were just as likely for those born in another country as those born in the U.S., according to a bilingual, online survey of 3,375 U.S. Latino adults conducted in March 2021. However, among immigrant Latinos, some groups were harder hit than others – a relatively high share (58%) of Latino immigrants without U.S. citizenship and without a green card say they or someone in their household has lost a job or wages since February 2020, compared with 45% of naturalized U.S. citizen immigrants who say this.1

Yet Latinos see better days ahead for themselves and the country, even if they have experienced hardship due to COVID-19. Most Latinos say they think the worst of the problems the country is facing from the outbreak are behind us, with similar majorities saying so among those who have had and not had someone close to them hospitalized or die due to the coronavirus. In addition, a slight majority of Latinos (54%) say they expect their personal financial situation will be better a year from now, with only modest differences between those in households that have and have not experienced a loss of jobs or wages since the start of the pandemic.
Terminology
The terms Hispanic and Latino are used interchangeably in this report.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term U.S. born refers to people who are U.S. citizens at birth, including people born in the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories, as well as those born elsewhere to at least one parent who is a U.S. citizen.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term foreign born refers to persons born outside of the United States to parents neither of whom was a U.S. citizen. The terms foreign born and immigrant are used interchangeably in this report.
Second generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with at least one first-generation, or immigrant, parent.

Third or higher generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with both parents born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories.

Over the course of the pandemic, Latinos have become more optimistic about the country. About half (49%) say they are satisfied with the nation’s direction, up from June 2020, when 20% said the same. This is the most satisfied Latinos have been with the nation’s direction since 2012, when 51% said so. At the same time, the share saying the worst of the pandemic is behind us as a nation is up sharply, from 23% in April 2020 to 65% in March 2021. Meanwhile, Latino adults are more likely today than before the pandemic to say the situation of U.S. Latinos has improved or stayed about the same over the past year, and they are less likely to say the situation of Latinos has worsened.

query:
Dans l’enquête, quel est le nombre exact de Latinos qui déclarent « Ils s’attendent à ce que leur situation
financière ainsi que celle de leur famille
soient meilleures dans un an » et appartiennent au groupe « Vivent dans un ménage ayant subi une
perte d’emploi ou une baisse de salaire
pendant la pandémie » ? Arrondissez la réponse à l’entier inférieur.

paragraphs.text: Plus d’un an après le début de la pandémie, les Latinos aux États-Unis déclarent que la COVID19 leur a nui, ainsi qu’à leurs proches, de nombreuses façons. Environ la moitié déclarent qu’un membre de leur famille ou un ami proche a été hospitalisé ou est décédé à cause du coronavirus, et une proportion similaire indiquent qu’eux-mêmes ou une personne de leur foyer ont perdu un emploi ou subi une baisse de salaire pendant la pandémie. Pourtant, malgré ces difficultés, les Latinos sont optimistes quant à l’avenir. Près des deux tiers estiment que le pire de l’épidémie de coronavirus est derrière le pays, et une majorité déclarent s’attendre à ce que leur situation financière et celle de leur famille s’améliorent au cours de l’année à venir.

Pendant la pandémie, les pertes d’emploi et les baisses de salaire dans les foyers latinos étaient tout aussi probables pour les personnes nées dans un autre pays que pour celles nées aux États-Unis, selon une enquête bilingue menée en ligne auprès de 3,375 adultes latinos aux États-Unis en mars 2021. Toutefois, parmi les immigrés latinos, certains groupes ont été plus durement touchés que d’autres : une proportion relativement élevée (58%) d’immigrés latinos n’ayant ni la citoyenneté américaine ni une carte verte déclarent qu’eux-mêmes ou une personne de leur foyer ont perdu un emploi ou subi une baisse de salaire depuis février 2020, contre 45% des immigrés naturalisés citoyens américains.1

Pourtant, les Latinos entrevoient des jours meilleurs pour eux-mêmes et pour le pays, même s’ils ont connu des difficultés dues à la COVID-19. La plupart des Latinos estiment que les pires problèmes auxquels le pays est confronté en raison de l’épidémie sont derrière nous ; des majorités similaires partagent cet avis, qu’ils aient eu ou non un proche hospitalisé ou décédé à cause du coronavirus. En outre, une courte majorité de Latinos (54%) déclarent s’attendre à ce que leur situation financière personnelle soit meilleure dans un an, avec seulement de faibles différences entre les personnes vivant dans des foyers ayant subi une perte d’emploi ou une baisse de salaire depuis le début de la pandémie et celles vivant dans des foyers n’en ayant pas subi.
Terminologie
Les termes « hispanique » et « latino » sont utilisés de manière interchangeable dans ce rapport.

Sauf indication contraire, le terme « né aux États-Unis » désigne les personnes qui sont citoyennes américaines à la naissance, y compris celles nées dans les 50 États américains, le district de Columbia, à Porto Rico ou dans d’autres territoires américains, ainsi que celles nées ailleurs dont au moins un parent est citoyen américain.

Sauf indication contraire, le terme « né à l’étranger » désigne les personnes nées hors des États-Unis de parents dont aucun n’était citoyen américain. Les termes « né à l’étranger » et « immigré » sont utilisés de manière interchangeable dans ce rapport.

La deuxième génération désigne les personnes nées dans les 50 États, le district de Columbia, à Porto Rico ou dans d’autres territoires américains, dont au moins un parent est de première génération, c’est-à-dire immigré.

La troisième génération ou les générations suivantes désignent les personnes nées dans les 50 États, le district de Columbia, à Porto Rico ou dans d’autres territoires américains, dont les deux parents sont nés dans les 50 États, le district de Columbia, à Porto Rico ou dans d’autres territoires américains.

Au fil de la pandémie, les Latinos sont devenus plus optimistes quant au pays. Environ la moitié (49%) se disent satisfaits de la direction prise par le pays, une proportion en hausse par rapport à juin 2020, lorsque 20% partageaient cet avis. Le niveau de satisfaction des Latinos à l’égard de la direction prise par le pays n’avait pas été aussi élevé depuis 2012, lorsque 51% se disaient satisfaits. Dans le même temps, la proportion de ceux qui estiment que le pire de la pandémie est derrière nous à l’échelle nationale a fortement augmenté, passant de 23% en avril 2020 à 65% en mars 2021. Par ailleurs, les adultes latinos sont aujourd’hui plus susceptibles qu’avant la pandémie de déclarer que la situation des Latinos aux États-Unis s’est améliorée ou est restée à peu près la même au cours de l’année écoulée, et moins susceptibles de déclarer qu’elle s’est dégradée.

query:
Wie hoch ist in der Umfrage die genaue Zahl der Latinos, die „Sie erwarten, dass ihre finanzielle
Situation und die ihrer Familie
in einem Jahr besser sein werden“ angeben und zur Gruppe „Leben in einem Haushalt mit
Arbeitsplatzverlust oder Gehaltseinbußen
während der Pandemie“ gehören? Runden Sie die Antwort auf die nächste ganze Zahl ab.

paragraphs.text: Mehr als ein Jahr nach Beginn der Pandemie sagen Latinos in den Vereinigten Staaten, dass COVID19 ihnen und ihren Angehörigen auf vielfältige Weise geschadet hat. Etwa die Hälfte gibt an, dass ein Familienmitglied oder ein enger Freund wegen des Coronavirus ins Krankenhaus eingeliefert wurde oder daran gestorben ist, und ein ähnlich großer Anteil sagt, dass sie selbst oder jemand in ihrem Haushalt während der Pandemie den Arbeitsplatz verloren oder Gehaltseinbußen hinnehmen mussten. Doch trotz dieser Schwierigkeiten blicken Latinos zuversichtlich in die Zukunft. Fast zwei Drittel sagen, dass das Land das Schlimmste des Coronavirus-Ausbruchs hinter sich hat, und eine Mehrheit erwartet, dass sich ihre finanzielle Situation und die ihrer Familie im Laufe des nächsten Jahres verbessern wird.

Arbeitsplatzverluste und Lohneinbußen in Latino-Haushalten während der Pandemie betrafen in einem anderen Land Geborene ebenso häufig wie in den USA Geborene. Dies geht aus einer zweisprachigen Online-Umfrage unter 3,375 erwachsenen Latinos in den USA hervor, die im März 2021 durchgeführt wurde. Unter den eingewanderten Latinos waren jedoch einige Gruppen stärker betroffen als andere: Ein vergleichsweise hoher Anteil (58%) der eingewanderten Latinos ohne US-Staatsbürgerschaft und ohne Green Card gibt an, dass sie selbst oder jemand in ihrem Haushalt seit Februar 2020 den Arbeitsplatz verloren oder Lohneinbußen erlitten haben, verglichen mit 45% der Einwanderer mit durch Einbürgerung erworbener US-Staatsbürgerschaft, die dies angeben.1

Dennoch sehen Latinos für sich selbst und das Land bessere Zeiten kommen, selbst wenn sie aufgrund von COVID-19 Schwierigkeiten erlebt haben. Die meisten Latinos glauben, dass das Schlimmste der Probleme, mit denen das Land aufgrund des Ausbruchs konfrontiert ist, hinter uns liegt. Ähnlich große Mehrheiten äußern diese Ansicht sowohl unter denjenigen, bei denen eine nahestehende Person wegen des Coronavirus ins Krankenhaus eingeliefert wurde oder daran gestorben ist, als auch unter denjenigen, die dies nicht erlebt haben. Darüber hinaus erwartet eine knappe Mehrheit der Latinos (54%), dass ihre persönliche finanzielle Situation in einem Jahr besser sein wird. Dabei gibt es nur geringe Unterschiede zwischen Angehörigen von Haushalten, die seit Beginn der Pandemie Arbeitsplatzverluste oder Lohneinbußen erlebt haben, und solchen, die dies nicht erlebt haben.
Terminologie
Die Begriffe Hispanic und Latino werden in diesem Bericht synonym verwendet.

Sofern nicht anders angegeben, bezeichnet der Begriff „in den USA geboren“ Personen, die von Geburt an US-Staatsbürger sind. Dazu gehören Personen, die in den 50 US-Bundesstaaten, im District of Columbia, in Puerto Rico oder in anderen US-Territorien geboren wurden, sowie Personen, die anderswo geboren wurden und bei denen mindestens ein Elternteil US-Staatsbürger ist.

Sofern nicht anders angegeben, bezeichnet der Begriff „im Ausland geboren“ Personen, die außerhalb der Vereinigten Staaten geboren wurden und deren Eltern beide keine US-Staatsbürger waren. Die Begriffe „im Ausland geboren“ und „Einwanderer“ werden in diesem Bericht synonym verwendet.

Die zweite Generation bezeichnet Personen, die in den 50 Bundesstaaten, im District of Columbia, in Puerto Rico oder in anderen US-Territorien geboren wurden und bei denen mindestens ein Elternteil der ersten Generation angehört, also eingewandert ist.

Die dritte oder eine spätere Generation bezeichnet Personen, die in den 50 Bundesstaaten, im District of Columbia, in Puerto Rico oder in anderen US-Territorien geboren wurden und deren Eltern beide in den 50 Bundesstaaten, im District of Columbia, in Puerto Rico oder in anderen US-Territorien geboren wurden.

Im Laufe der Pandemie sind Latinos im Hinblick auf das Land optimistischer geworden. Etwa die Hälfte (49%) gibt an, mit der Richtung, in die sich das Land entwickelt, zufrieden zu sein. Das ist ein Anstieg gegenüber Juni 2020, als 20% dasselbe sagten. So zufrieden mit der Richtung, in die sich das Land entwickelt, waren Latinos zuletzt 2012, als 51% dies angaben. Gleichzeitig ist der Anteil derjenigen, die sagen, dass wir als Nation das Schlimmste der Pandemie hinter uns haben, deutlich gestiegen: von 23% im April 2020 auf 65% im März 2021. Unterdessen geben erwachsene Latinos heute häufiger als vor der Pandemie an, dass sich die Lage der Latinos in den USA im vergangenen Jahr verbessert hat oder etwa gleich geblieben ist, und seltener, dass sich die Lage der Latinos verschlechtert hat.

query:
In the survey, what is the exact number of Latinos who report They expect their financial
situation as well as their family’s
to be better a year from now and belong to the group Live in a household with
job or wage loss during
the pandemic? Round the answer down to the nearest integer.

paragraphs.text: More than a year into the pandemic, Latinos in the United States say COVID19 has harmed them and their loved ones in many ways. About half say a family member or close friend has been hospitalized or died from the coronavirus, and a similar share say they or someone in their household has lost a job or taken a pay cut during the pandemic. Yet amid these hardships, Latinos are upbeat about the future. Nearly twothirds say the worst of the coronavirus outbreak is behind the country, and a majority say they expect their financial situation and that of their family to improve over the next year.

Job and wage losses in Latino households during the pandemic were just as likely for those born in another country as those born in the U.S., according to a bilingual, online survey of 3,375 U.S. Latino adults conducted in March 2021. However, among immigrant Latinos, some groups were harder hit than others – a relatively high share (58%) of Latino immigrants without U.S. citizenship and without a green card say they or someone in their household has lost a job or wages since February 2020, compared with 45% of naturalized U.S. citizen immigrants who say this.1

Yet Latinos see better days ahead for themselves and the country, even if they have experienced hardship due to COVID-19. Most Latinos say they think the worst of the problems the country is facing from the outbreak are behind us, with similar majorities saying so among those who have had and not had someone close to them hospitalized or die due to the coronavirus. In addition, a slight majority of Latinos (54%) say they expect their personal financial situation will be better a year from now, with only modest differences between those in households that have and have not experienced a loss of jobs or wages since the start of the pandemic.
Terminology
The terms Hispanic and Latino are used interchangeably in this report.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term U.S. born refers to people who are U.S. citizens at birth, including people born in the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories, as well as those born elsewhere to at least one parent who is a U.S. citizen.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term foreign born refers to persons born outside of the United States to parents neither of whom was a U.S. citizen. The terms foreign born and immigrant are used interchangeably in this report.
Second generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with at least one first-generation, or immigrant, parent.

Third or higher generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with both parents born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories.

Over the course of the pandemic, Latinos have become more optimistic about the country. About half (49%) say they are satisfied with the nation’s direction, up from June 2020, when 20% said the same. This is the most satisfied Latinos have been with the nation’s direction since 2012, when 51% said so. At the same time, the share saying the worst of the pandemic is behind us as a nation is up sharply, from 23% in April 2020 to 65% in March 2021. Meanwhile, Latino adults are more likely today than before the pandemic to say the situation of U.S. Latinos has improved or stayed about the same over the past year, and they are less likely to say the situation of Latinos has worsened.

query:
En la encuesta, ¿cuál es el número exacto de latinos que afirman «Esperan que su situación económica,
así como la de su familia,
mejore dentro de un año» y pertenecen al grupo «Viven en un hogar con
pérdida de empleo o reducción salarial
durante la pandemia»? Redondea la respuesta hacia abajo al entero más cercano.

paragraphs.text: Más de un año después del inicio de la pandemia, los latinos en Estados Unidos afirman que la COVID19 los ha perjudicado a ellos y a sus seres queridos de muchas maneras. Aproximadamente la mitad dice que un familiar o un amigo cercano ha sido hospitalizado o ha fallecido a causa del coronavirus, y una proporción similar afirma que ellos o alguien de su hogar ha perdido un empleo o ha sufrido una reducción salarial durante la pandemia. Sin embargo, en medio de estas dificultades, los latinos se muestran optimistas respecto al futuro. Casi dos tercios dicen que el país ya ha dejado atrás lo peor del brote de coronavirus, y una mayoría afirma que espera que su situación económica y la de su familia mejoren durante el próximo año.

Las pérdidas de empleo y las reducciones salariales en los hogares latinos durante la pandemia fueron igual de probables entre los nacidos en otro país que entre los nacidos en Estados Unidos, según una encuesta bilingüe en línea realizada en marzo de 2021 a 3,375 adultos latinos de Estados Unidos. Sin embargo, entre los latinos inmigrantes, algunos grupos se vieron más afectados que otros: una proporción relativamente alta (58%) de inmigrantes latinos sin ciudadanía estadounidense ni tarjeta de residencia permanente dice que ellos o alguien de su hogar ha perdido un empleo o ha sufrido una reducción salarial desde febrero de 2020, en comparación con el 45% de los inmigrantes naturalizados como ciudadanos estadounidenses que afirman lo mismo.1

Sin embargo, los latinos prevén días mejores para ellos y para el país, incluso si han experimentado dificultades debido a la COVID-19. La mayoría de los latinos dice que cree que ya hemos dejado atrás lo peor de los problemas que el país enfrenta a causa del brote, con mayorías similares que opinan así tanto entre quienes han tenido a alguien cercano hospitalizado o fallecido a causa del coronavirus como entre quienes no. Además, una ligera mayoría de los latinos (54%) afirma que espera que su situación económica personal sea mejor dentro de un año, con diferencias apenas modestas entre quienes viven en hogares que han sufrido pérdidas de empleo o reducciones salariales desde el inicio de la pandemia y quienes no.
Terminología
Los términos hispano y latino se utilizan indistintamente en este informe.

Salvo que se indique lo contrario, el término nacido en Estados Unidos se refiere a las personas que son ciudadanas estadounidenses de nacimiento, incluidas las nacidas en los 50 estados de Estados Unidos, el Distrito de Columbia, Puerto Rico u otros territorios estadounidenses, así como las nacidas en otros lugares con al menos un progenitor que sea ciudadano estadounidense.

Salvo que se indique lo contrario, el término nacido en el extranjero se refiere a las personas nacidas fuera de Estados Unidos cuyos progenitores no eran ciudadanos estadounidenses. Los términos nacido en el extranjero e inmigrante se utilizan indistintamente en este informe.

Segunda generación se refiere a las personas nacidas en los 50 estados, el Distrito de Columbia, Puerto Rico u otros territorios estadounidenses con al menos un progenitor de primera generación, o inmigrante.

Tercera generación o posterior se refiere a las personas nacidas en los 50 estados, el Distrito de Columbia, Puerto Rico u otros territorios estadounidenses cuyos dos progenitores nacieron en los 50 estados, el Distrito de Columbia, Puerto Rico u otros territorios estadounidenses.

A lo largo de la pandemia, los latinos se han vuelto más optimistas respecto al país. Aproximadamente la mitad (49%) dice estar satisfecha con el rumbo del país, una proporción mayor que en junio de 2020, cuando el 20% afirmaba lo mismo. Este es el mayor nivel de satisfacción de los latinos con el rumbo del país desde 2012, cuando el 51% lo afirmaba. Al mismo tiempo, la proporción que dice que, como nación, ya hemos dejado atrás lo peor de la pandemia ha aumentado considerablemente, del 23% en abril de 2020 al 65% en marzo de 2021. Mientras tanto, los adultos latinos son más propensos hoy que antes de la pandemia a decir que la situación de los latinos en Estados Unidos ha mejorado o se ha mantenido prácticamente igual durante el último año, y son menos propensos a decir que la situación de los latinos ha empeorado.

query:

situation as well as their family’s
to be better a year from now and belong to the group Live in a household with
job or wage loss during
the pandemic? Round the answer down to the nearest integer.

paragraphs.text: More than a year into the pandemic, Latinos in the United States say COVID19 has harmed them and their loved ones in many ways. About half say a family member or close friend has been hospitalized or died from the coronavirus, and a similar share say they or someone in their household has lost a job or taken a pay cut during the pandemic. Yet amid these hardships, Latinos are upbeat about the future. Nearly twothirds say the worst of the coronavirus outbreak is behind the country, and a majority say they expect their financial situation and that of their family to improve over the next year.

Job and wage losses in Latino households during the pandemic were just as likely for those born in another country as those born in the U.S., according to a bilingual, online survey of 3,375 U.S. Latino adults conducted in March 2021. However, among immigrant Latinos, some groups were harder hit than others – a relatively high share (58%) of Latino immigrants without U.S. citizenship and without a green card say they or someone in their household has lost a job or wages since February 2020, compared with 45% of naturalized U.S. citizen immigrants who say this.1

Yet Latinos see better days ahead for themselves and the country, even if they have experienced hardship due to COVID-19. Most Latinos say they think the worst of the problems the country is facing from the outbreak are behind us, with similar majorities saying so among those who have had and not had someone close to them hospitalized or die due to the coronavirus. In addition, a slight majority of Latinos (54%) say they expect their personal financial situation will be better a year from now, with only modest differences between those in households that have and have not experienced a loss of jobs or wages since the start of the pandemic.
Terminology
The terms Hispanic and Latino are used interchangeably in this report.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term U.S. born refers to people who are U.S. citizens at birth, including people born in the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories, as well as those born elsewhere to at least one parent who is a U.S. citizen.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term foreign born refers to persons born outside of the United States to parents neither of whom was a U.S. citizen. The terms foreign born and immigrant are used interchangeably in this report.
Second generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with at least one first-generation, or immigrant, parent.

Third or higher generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with both parents born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories.

Over the course of the pandemic, Latinos have become more optimistic about the country. About half (49%) say they are satisfied with the nation’s direction, up from June 2020, when 20% said the same. query:
Na pesquisa, qual é o número exato de latinos que relatam "Esperam que sua situação financeira,
assim como a de sua família,
esteja melhor daqui a um ano" e pertencem ao grupo "Vivem em um domicílio com
perda de emprego ou salário durante
a pandemia"? Arredonde a resposta para baixo até o inteiro mais próximo.

paragraphs.text: Mais de um ano após o início da pandemia, os latinos nos Estados Unidos dizem que a COVID19 prejudicou a eles e aos seus entes queridos de muitas maneiras. Cerca de metade diz que um familiar ou amigo próximo foi hospitalizado ou morreu em decorrência do coronavírus, e uma proporção semelhante diz que eles próprios ou alguém em seu domicílio perdeu o emprego ou sofreu uma redução salarial durante a pandemia. No entanto, em meio a essas dificuldades, os latinos estão otimistas quanto ao futuro. Quase dois terços dizem que o pior do surto de coronavírus já passou no país, e a maioria diz esperar que sua situação financeira e a de sua família melhorem ao longo do próximo ano.

As perdas de empregos e as reduções salariais nos domicílios latinos durante a pandemia foram tão prováveis entre os nascidos em outro país quanto entre os nascidos nos EUA, segundo uma pesquisa on-line bilíngue com 3,375 adultos latinos nos EUA, realizada em março de 2021. No entanto, entre os latinos imigrantes, alguns grupos foram mais afetados do que outros — uma proporção relativamente elevada (58%) de imigrantes latinos sem cidadania americana e sem green card diz que eles próprios ou alguém em seu domicílio perdeu o emprego ou sofreu uma redução salarial desde fevereiro de 2020, em comparação com 45% dos imigrantes naturalizados cidadãos americanos que dizem o mesmo.1

Ainda assim, os latinos veem dias melhores pela frente para si mesmos e para o país, mesmo que tenham enfrentado dificuldades devido à COVID-19. A maioria dos latinos diz acreditar que o pior dos problemas que o país enfrenta em decorrência do surto já passou, com maiorias semelhantes expressando essa opinião tanto entre aqueles que tiveram alguém próximo hospitalizado ou falecido devido ao coronavírus quanto entre aqueles que não tiveram. Além disso, uma pequena maioria dos latinos (54%) diz esperar que sua situação financeira pessoal esteja melhor daqui a um ano, com apenas pequenas diferenças entre aqueles em domicílios que sofreram perdas de empregos ou reduções salariais desde o início da pandemia e aqueles em domicílios que não sofreram essas perdas.
Terminologia
Os termos hispânico e latino são usados de forma intercambiável neste relatório.

Salvo indicação em contrário, o termo nascido nos EUA refere-se às pessoas que são cidadãs americanas desde o nascimento, incluindo pessoas nascidas nos 50 estados dos EUA, no Distrito de Colúmbia, em Porto Rico ou em outros territórios dos EUA, bem como aquelas nascidas em outros lugares cujo pai ou mãe, ou ambos, tenham cidadania americana.

Salvo indicação em contrário, o termo nascido no exterior refere-se às pessoas nascidas fora dos Estados Unidos cujos pais não tinham cidadania americana. Os termos nascido no exterior e imigrante são usados de forma intercambiável neste relatório.

Segunda geração refere-se às pessoas nascidas nos 50 estados, no Distrito de Colúmbia, em Porto Rico ou em outros territórios dos EUA cujo pai ou mãe, ou ambos, sejam de primeira geração, ou imigrantes.

Terceira geração ou posterior refere-se às pessoas nascidas nos 50 estados, no Distrito de Colúmbia, em Porto Rico ou em outros territórios dos EUA cujos pais tenham ambos nascido nos 50 estados, no Distrito de Colúmbia, em Porto Rico ou em outros territórios dos EUA.

Ao longo da pandemia, os latinos se tornaram mais otimistas em relação ao país. Cerca de metade (49%) diz estar satisfeita com o rumo da nação, uma proporção maior do que em junho de 2020, quando 20% disseram o mesmo. Este é o maior nível de satisfação dos latinos com o rumo da nação desde 2012, quando 51% disseram estar satisfeitos. Ao mesmo tempo, a proporção dos que dizem que o pior da pandemia já passou para nós, como nação, aumentou acentuadamente, de 23% em abril de 2020 para 65% em março de 2021. Enquanto isso, os adultos latinos estão mais propensos hoje do que antes da pandemia a dizer que a situação dos latinos nos EUA melhorou ou permaneceu praticamente igual ao longo do último ano, e estão menos propensos a dizer que a situação dos latinos piorou.

query:
Каково точное число латиноамериканцев в опросе, которые сообщают, что Ожидают, что их финансовое
положение, а также положение их семьи
через год улучшится, и относятся к группе «Живут в домохозяйстве, где были
потеря работы или зарплаты во время
пандемии»? Округлите ответ вниз до ближайшего целого числа.

paragraphs.text: Спустя более года после начала пандемии латиноамериканцы в Соединённых Штатах говорят, что COVID19 во многих отношениях навредил им и их близким. Около половины говорят, что член их семьи или близкий друг был госпитализирован или умер из-за коронавируса, и примерно такая же доля сообщает, что они сами или кто-то из членов их домохозяйства потеряли работу или столкнулись с сокращением заработной платы во время пандемии. Однако, несмотря на эти трудности, латиноамериканцы с оптимизмом смотрят в будущее. Почти две трети говорят, что худший этап вспышки коронавируса для страны уже позади, а большинство ожидает улучшения своего финансового положения и финансового положения своей семьи в течение следующего года.

Согласно двуязычному онлайн-опросу 3,375 взрослых латиноамериканцев в США, проведённому в марте 2021 года, потеря работы и сокращение заработной платы в латиноамериканских домохозяйствах во время пандемии были столь же вероятны среди родившихся в другой стране, как и среди родившихся в США. Однако среди латиноамериканских иммигрантов некоторые группы пострадали сильнее других: относительно высокая доля (58%) латиноамериканских иммигрантов, не имеющих ни гражданства США, ни грин-карты, говорит, что они сами или кто-то из членов их домохозяйства потеряли работу или заработок с февраля 2020 года, тогда как среди иммигрантов, получивших гражданство США путём натурализации, об этом говорят 45%.1

Тем не менее латиноамериканцы считают, что лучшие дни для них самих и для страны ещё впереди, даже если они столкнулись с трудностями из-за COVID-19. Большинство латиноамериканцев полагает, что худшие проблемы, с которыми страна столкнулась из-за вспышки заболевания, уже позади; об этом говорит примерно одинаковое большинство как среди тех, у кого кто-то из близких был госпитализирован или умер из-за коронавируса, так и среди тех, у кого такого не было. Кроме того, небольшое большинство латиноамериканцев (54%) ожидает, что через год их личное финансовое положение улучшится, причём различия между представителями домохозяйств, столкнувшихся и не столкнувшихся с потерей работы или заработка с начала пандемии, невелики.
Терминология
Термины «испаноязычный» и «латиноамериканец» используются в этом отчёте как взаимозаменяемые.

Если не указано иное, термин «родившиеся в США» относится к людям, являющимся гражданами США по рождению, включая людей, родившихся в 50 штатах США, округе Колумбия, Пуэрто-Рико или на других территориях США, а также родившихся в других местах, у которых хотя бы один из родителей является гражданином США.

Если не указано иное, термин «родившиеся за рубежом» относится к лицам, родившимся за пределами Соединённых Штатов у родителей, ни один из которых не был гражданином США. Термины «родившиеся за рубежом» и «иммигранты» используются в этом отчёте как взаимозаменяемые.

Ко второму поколению относятся люди, родившиеся в 50 штатах, округе Колумбия, Пуэрто-Рико или на других территориях США, у которых хотя бы один из родителей относится к первому поколению, то есть является иммигрантом.

К третьему или последующим поколениям относятся люди, родившиеся в 50 штатах, округе Колумбия, Пуэрто-Рико или на других территориях США, оба родителя которых родились в 50 штатах, округе Колумбия, Пуэрто-Рико или на других территориях США.

За время пандемии латиноамериканцы стали более оптимистично смотреть на положение дел в стране. Около половины (49%) говорят, что довольны направлением, в котором движется страна; эта доля выросла по сравнению с июнем 2020 года, когда то же самое говорили 20%. Это самый высокий уровень удовлетворённости латиноамериканцев направлением развития страны с 2012 года, когда об этом говорили 51%. В то же время доля тех, кто считает, что худший этап пандемии для страны уже позади, резко выросла: с 23% в апреле 2020 года до 65% в марте 2021 года. При этом сегодня взрослые латиноамериканцы чаще, чем до пандемии, говорят, что положение латиноамериканцев в США за последний год улучшилось или осталось примерно прежним, и реже говорят, что оно ухудшилось.

然而，即便因COVID-19经历了困难，拉丁裔仍认为自己和国家将迎来更好的日子。大多数拉丁裔表示，他们认为国家因疫情暴发而面临的最严重问题已经过去；无论是否有亲近的人因感染冠状病毒而住院或去世，持这一看法的人都占多数，且比例相近。此外，略多于半数的拉丁裔（54%）表示，他们预计一年后个人财务状况会有所改善；自疫情开始以来家庭经历过失业或工资损失的人与未经历过这些情况的人之间，仅存在不大的差异。
术语
本报告中，西班牙裔与拉丁裔两个术语可互换使用。
除非另有说明，“美国出生”一词指生来即为美国公民的人，包括出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土的人，以及出生于其他地方但父母中至少一方为美国公民的人。
除非另有说明，“外国出生”一词指出生于美国境外且父母双方均非美国公民的人。本报告中，“外国出生”与“移民”两个术语可互换使用。
第二代指出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土，且父母中至少一方为第一代移民的人。
第三代或更高世代指出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土，且父母双方均出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土的人。

在疫情期间，拉丁裔对国家变得更加乐观。约一半（49%）表示，他们对国家的发展方向感到满意，高于2020年六月的20%。这是自2012年以来拉丁裔对国家发展方向最满意的一次，当时有51%的人表示满意。与此同时，认为全国已经度过疫情最严重阶段的人所占比例大幅上升，从2020年四月的23%升至2021年三月的65%。此外，与疫情前相比，如今拉丁裔成年人更有可能表示，美国拉丁裔的处境在过去一年有所改善或基本保持不变，而表示拉丁裔处境恶化的可能性则有所降低。

query:
في المسح، ما العدد الدقيق للاتينيين الذين يفيدون بأنهم يتوقعون أن يتحسن وضعهم المالي
وكذلك وضع أسرهم المالي
بعد عام من الآن وينتمون إلى مجموعة «يعيشون في أسرة معيشية شهدت
فقدان وظائف أو أجور خلال
الجائحة»؟ قرّب الإجابة إلى أقرب عدد صحيح أدنى.

paragraphs.text: بعد مرور أكثر من عام على بدء الجائحة، يقول اللاتينيون في الولايات المتحدة إن كوفيد19 أضر بهم وبأحبائهم بطرق عديدة. ويقول نحو نصفهم إن أحد أفراد أسرهم أو أصدقائهم المقربين أُدخل المستشفى أو توفي بسبب فيروس كورونا، وتقول نسبة مماثلة إنهم أو شخصًا من أفراد أسرهم المعيشية فقدوا وظيفة أو تعرضوا لخفض في الأجر خلال الجائحة. ومع ذلك، يبدي اللاتينيون تفاؤلًا بالمستقبل وسط هذه المصاعب. ويقول ما يقرب من ثلثيهم إن البلاد تجاوزت أسوأ مراحل تفشي فيروس كورونا، وتقول أغلبية إنهم يتوقعون تحسن وضعهم المالي ووضع أسرهم خلال العام المقبل.

كان احتمال فقدان الوظائف والأجور في الأسر المعيشية اللاتينية خلال الجائحة متساويًا بين المولودين في بلد آخر والمولودين في الولايات المتحدة، وفقًا لاستطلاع ثنائي اللغة أُجري عبر الإنترنت وشمل 3,375 من البالغين اللاتينيين في الولايات المتحدة في مارس 2021. ومع ذلك، تضررت بعض الفئات بين المهاجرين اللاتينيين أكثر من غيرها؛ إذ تقول نسبة مرتفعة نسبيًا (58%) من المهاجرين اللاتينيين الذين لا يحملون الجنسية الأمريكية ولا البطاقة الخضراء إنهم أو شخصًا من أفراد أسرهم المعيشية فقدوا وظيفة أو أجورًا منذ فبراير 2020، مقارنةً بنسبة 45% من المهاجرين المتجنسين بالجنسية الأمريكية الذين يقولون ذلك.1

ومع ذلك، يرى اللاتينيون أن أيامًا أفضل تنتظرهم وتنتظر البلاد، حتى إن كانوا قد عانوا من مصاعب بسبب كوفيد-19. ويقول معظم اللاتينيين إنهم يعتقدون أننا تجاوزنا أسوأ المشكلات التي تواجهها البلاد جراء تفشي المرض، وتقول ذلك أغلبيتان متقاربتان بين من أُدخل أحد المقربين منهم المستشفى أو توفي بسبب فيروس كورونا ومن لم يحدث لهم ذلك. وبالإضافة إلى ذلك، تقول أغلبية طفيفة من اللاتينيين (54%) إنهم يتوقعون أن يكون وضعهم المالي الشخصي أفضل بعد عام من الآن، مع وجود فروق محدودة فقط بين المنتمين إلى أسر معيشية شهدت فقدان وظائف أو أجور منذ بداية الجائحة والمنتمين إلى أسر لم تشهد ذلك.
المصطلحات
يُستخدم مصطلحا «هسباني» و«لاتيني» بالتبادل في هذا التقرير.

ما لم يُذكر خلاف ذلك، يشير مصطلح «المولودون في الولايات المتحدة» إلى الأشخاص الذين يحملون الجنسية الأمريكية منذ الولادة، بمن فيهم المولودون في الولايات الأمريكية الـ50 أو مقاطعة كولومبيا أو بورتوريكو أو غيرها من الأقاليم الأمريكية، وكذلك المولودون في أماكن أخرى لأب أو أم، على الأقل، يحمل الجنسية الأمريكية.

ما لم يُذكر خلاف ذلك، يشير مصطلح «المولودون في الخارج» إلى الأشخاص المولودين خارج الولايات المتحدة لأبوين لم يكن أي منهما يحمل الجنسية الأمريكية. ويُستخدم مصطلحا «المولودون في الخارج» و«المهاجرون» بالتبادل في هذا التقرير.
يشير مصطلح «الجيل الثاني» إلى الأشخاص المولودين في الولايات الـ50 أو مقاطعة كولومبيا أو بورتوريكو أو غيرها من الأقاليم الأمريكية، ممن ينتمي أحد والديهم على الأقل إلى الجيل الأول، أي المهاجرين.

يشير مصطلح «الجيل الثالث أو الأجيال اللاحقة» إلى الأشخاص المولودين في الولايات الـ50 أو مقاطعة كولومبيا أو بورتوريكو أو غيرها من الأقاليم الأمريكية، والذين وُلد كلا والديهم في الولايات الـ50 أو مقاطعة كولومبيا أو بورتوريكو أو غيرها من الأقاليم الأمريكية.

على مدار الجائحة، أصبح اللاتينيون أكثر تفاؤلًا بشأن البلاد. ويقول نحو نصفهم (49%) إنهم راضون عن الاتجاه الذي تسلكه البلاد، بزيادة عما كان عليه الحال في يونيو 2020، حين قال 20% الشيء نفسه. وهذا هو أعلى مستوى لرضا اللاتينيين عن الاتجاه الذي تسلكه البلاد منذ 2012، حين قال ذلك 51%. وفي الوقت نفسه، ارتفعت بشدة نسبة من يقولون إننا تجاوزنا، بوصفنا أمة، أسوأ مراحل الجائحة، من 23% في أبريل 2020 إلى 65% في مارس 2021. وفي غضون ذلك، أصبح البالغون اللاتينيون اليوم أكثر ميلًا مما كانوا عليه قبل الجائحة إلى القول إن وضع اللاتينيين في الولايات المتحدة تحسن أو بقي على حاله تقريبًا خلال العام الماضي، وأقل ميلًا إلى القول إن وضع اللاتينيين قد ساء.

query:
In the survey, what is the exact number of Latinos who report They expect their financial
situation as well as their family’s
to be better a year from now and belong to the group Live in a household with
job or wage loss during
the pandemic? Round the answer down to the nearest integer.

paragraphs.text: More than a year into the pandemic, Latinos in the United States say COVID19 has harmed them and their loved ones in many ways. About half say a family member or close friend has been hospitalized or died from the coronavirus, and a similar share say they or someone in their household has lost a job or taken a pay cut during the pandemic. Yet amid these hardships, Latinos are upbeat about the future. Nearly twothirds say the worst of the coronavirus outbreak is behind the country, and a majority say they expect their financial situation and that of their family to improve over the next year.

Job and wage losses in Latino households during the pandemic were just as likely for those born in another country as those born in the U.S., according to a bilingual, online survey of 3,375 U.S. Latino adults conducted in March 2021. However, among immigrant Latinos, some groups were harder hit than others – a relatively high share (58%) of Latino immigrants without U.S. citizenship and without a green card say they or someone in their household has lost a job or wages since February 2020, compared with 45% of naturalized U.S. citizen immigrants who say this.1

Yet Latinos see better days ahead for themselves and the country, even if they have experienced hardship due to COVID-19. Most Latinos say they think the worst of the problems the country is facing from the outbreak are behind us, with similar majorities saying so among those who have had and not had someone close to them hospitalized or die due to the coronavirus. In addition, a slight majority of Latinos (54%) say they expect their personal financial situation will be better a year from now, with only modest differences between those in households that have and have not experienced a loss of jobs or wages since the start of the pandemic.
Terminology
The terms Hispanic and Latino are used interchangeably in this report.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term U.S. born refers to people who are U.S. citizens at birth, including people born in the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories, as well as those born elsewhere to at least one parent who is a U.S. citizen.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term foreign born refers to persons born outside of the United States to parents neither of whom was a U.S. citizen. The terms foreign born and immigrant are used interchangeably in this report.
Second generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with at least one first-generation, or immigrant, parent.

Third or higher generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with both parents born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories.

Over the course of the pandemic, Latinos have become more optimistic about the country. About half (49%) say they are satisfied with the nation’s direction, up from June 2020, when 20% said the same. This is the most satisfied Latinos have been with the nation’s direction since 2012, when 51% said so. At the same time, the share saying the worst of the pandemic is behind us as a nation is up sharply, from 23% in April 2020 to 65% in March 2021. Meanwhile, Latino adults are more likely today than before the pandemic to say the situation of U.S. Latinos has improved or stayed about the same over the past year, and they are less likely to say the situation of Latinos has worsened.

query:
सर्वेक्षण में, यह कहने वाले कि "उन्हें उम्मीद है कि आज से एक साल बाद
उनकी और उनके परिवार की
आर्थिक स्थिति बेहतर होगी" और "ऐसे घर में रहते हैं जहाँ
महामारी के दौरान नौकरी गई
या वेतन घटा" समूह में आने वाले लातिनो की सटीक संख्या क्या है? उत्तर को नीचे की ओर निकटतम पूर्णांक तक पूर्णांकित करें।

paragraphs.text: महामारी शुरू हुए एक वर्ष से अधिक समय बीतने के बाद, संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका में लातिनो लोगों का कहना है कि कोविड19 ने उन्हें और उनके प्रियजनों को कई तरह से नुकसान पहुँचाया है। लगभग आधे लोगों का कहना है कि उनके परिवार के किसी सदस्य या करीबी मित्र को कोरोनावायरस के कारण अस्पताल में भर्ती होना पड़ा या उसकी मृत्यु हो गई, और लगभग इतने ही लोगों का कहना है कि महामारी के दौरान उनकी या उनके घर के किसी व्यक्ति की नौकरी चली गई या वेतन में कटौती हुई। फिर भी, इन कठिनाइयों के बीच लातिनो लोग भविष्य को लेकर आशावादी हैं। लगभग दो-तिहाई लोगों का कहना है कि देश कोरोनावायरस प्रकोप के सबसे बुरे दौर से गुजर चुका है, और बहुमत का कहना है कि उन्हें अगले वर्ष के दौरान अपनी और अपने परिवार की आर्थिक स्थिति में सुधार होने की उम्मीद है।

मार्च 2021 में अमेरिका के 3,375 लातिनो वयस्कों के बीच किए गए एक द्विभाषी ऑनलाइन सर्वेक्षण के अनुसार, महामारी के दौरान लातिनो परिवारों में नौकरी और वेतन का नुकसान होने की संभावना दूसरे देश में जन्मे लोगों के लिए उतनी ही थी जितनी अमेरिका में जन्मे लोगों के लिए। हालांकि, आप्रवासी लातिनो लोगों में कुछ समूह दूसरों की तुलना में अधिक प्रभावित हुए — अमेरिकी नागरिकता और ग्रीन कार्ड, दोनों से वंचित लातिनो आप्रवासियों के अपेक्षाकृत बड़े हिस्से (58%) का कहना है कि फरवरी 2020 के बाद उनकी या उनके घर के किसी व्यक्ति की नौकरी चली गई या वेतन का नुकसान हुआ, जबकि देशीयकरण के माध्यम से अमेरिकी नागरिक बने आप्रवासियों में ऐसा कहने वालों का हिस्सा 45% है।1

फिर भी, लातिनो लोगों को अपने और देश के लिए आगे बेहतर दिन दिखाई देते हैं, भले ही उन्होंने कोविड-19 के कारण कठिनाइयों का सामना किया हो। अधिकांश लातिनो लोगों का कहना है कि उनके विचार में देश प्रकोप के कारण सामने आई समस्याओं के सबसे बुरे दौर से गुजर चुका है। जिन लोगों के किसी करीबी को कोरोनावायरस के कारण अस्पताल में भर्ती होना पड़ा या उसकी मृत्यु हुई और जिनके साथ ऐसा नहीं हुआ, दोनों समूहों में लगभग समान बहुमत यह बात कहता है। इसके अतिरिक्त, लातिनो लोगों के मामूली बहुमत (54%) का कहना है कि उन्हें उम्मीद है कि अब से एक वर्ष बाद उनकी व्यक्तिगत आर्थिक स्थिति बेहतर होगी। महामारी की शुरुआत के बाद से नौकरी या वेतन के नुकसान का सामना करने वाले परिवारों और ऐसा नुकसान न झेलने वाले परिवारों के लोगों के बीच इस मामले में केवल मामूली अंतर हैं।
शब्दावली
इस रिपोर्ट में हिस्पैनिक और लातिनो शब्दों का प्रयोग एक-दूसरे के स्थान पर किया गया है।

जब तक अन्यथा उल्लेख न किया गया हो, अमेरिका में जन्मे शब्द का अर्थ उन लोगों से है जो जन्म से अमेरिकी नागरिक हैं। इनमें अमेरिका के 50 राज्यों, डिस्ट्रिक्ट ऑफ कोलंबिया, प्यूर्टो रिको या अन्य अमेरिकी क्षेत्रों में जन्मे लोग, साथ ही अन्य स्थानों पर जन्मे वे लोग भी शामिल हैं जिनके माता-पिता में से कम से कम एक अमेरिकी नागरिक है।

जब तक अन्यथा उल्लेख न किया गया हो, विदेश में जन्मे शब्द का अर्थ उन व्यक्तियों से है जिनका जन्म संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका के बाहर हुआ और जिनके माता-पिता में से कोई भी अमेरिकी नागरिक नहीं था। इस रिपोर्ट में विदेश में जन्मे और आप्रवासी शब्दों का प्रयोग एक-दूसरे के स्थान पर किया गया है।

दूसरी पीढ़ी का अर्थ उन लोगों से है जिनका जन्म 50 राज्यों, डिस्ट्रिक्ट ऑफ कोलंबिया, प्यूर्टो रिको या अन्य अमेरिकी क्षेत्रों में हुआ और जिनके माता-पिता में से कम से कम एक पहली पीढ़ी का, या आप्रवासी, है।

तीसरी या उससे आगे की पीढ़ी का अर्थ उन लोगों से है जिनका जन्म 50 राज्यों, डिस्ट्रिक्ट ऑफ कोलंबिया, प्यूर्टो रिको या अन्य अमेरिकी क्षेत्रों में हुआ और जिनके माता-पिता दोनों का जन्म 50 राज्यों, डिस्ट्रिक्ट ऑफ कोलंबिया, प्यूर्टो रिको या अन्य अमेरिकी क्षेत्रों में हुआ।

महामारी के दौरान लातिनो लोग देश को लेकर अधिक आशावादी हुए हैं। लगभग आधे (49%) लोगों का कहना है कि वे देश की दिशा से संतुष्ट हैं, जो जून 2020 की तुलना में अधिक है, जब 20% ने यही बात कही थी। 2012 के बाद से लातिनो लोगों में देश की दिशा को लेकर संतुष्टि का यह सबसे ऊँचा स्तर है; तब 51% ने ऐसा कहा था। साथ ही, यह कहने वालों का हिस्सा तेजी से बढ़ा है कि एक राष्ट्र के रूप में हम महामारी के सबसे बुरे दौर से गुजर चुके हैं — अप्रैल 2020 में 23% से बढ़कर मार्च 2021 में 65% हो गया है। इस बीच, महामारी से पहले की तुलना में आज लातिनो वयस्कों के यह कहने की संभावना अधिक है कि पिछले वर्ष के दौरान अमेरिका में लातिनो लोगों की स्थिति में सुधार हुआ है या वह लगभग वैसी ही बनी रही है, और उनके यह कहने की संभावना कम है कि लातिनो लोगों की स्थिति बिगड़ी है।

query:
在调查中，表示他们预计一年后自己
及家人的财务状况
会有所改善且属于所在家庭在疫情期间
有人失业
或工资减少群体的拉丁裔确切人数是多少？将答案向下取整到最接近的整数。

paragraphs.text: 疫情暴发一年多以来，美国拉丁裔表示，COVID19在许多方面伤害了他们及其亲友。约一半的人表示，有家人或密友因感染冠状病毒而住院或去世，另有相近比例的人表示，他们本人或家中有人在疫情期间失业或被减薪。然而，尽管面临这些困难，拉丁裔仍对未来持乐观态度。近三分之二的人表示，美国已经度过了冠状病毒疫情最严重的阶段，多数人表示，他们预计自己及家人的财务状况将在未来一年有所改善。

根据2021年三月对3,375名美国拉丁裔成年人开展的一项双语在线调查，在疫情期间，出生于其他国家的拉丁裔家庭与出生于美国的拉丁裔家庭遭遇失业和工资损失的可能性相同。然而，在拉丁裔移民中，一些群体受到的冲击比其他群体更大：既没有美国公民身份也没有绿卡的拉丁裔移民中，表示自2020年二月以来自己或家中有人失业或遭遇工资损失的比例相对较高，为58%；相比之下，已归化为美国公民的移民中，这一比例为45%。1
然而，即便因COVID-19经历了困难，拉丁裔仍认为自己和国家将迎来更好的日子。大多数拉丁裔表示，他们认为国家因疫情暴发而面临的最严重问题已经过去；无论是否有亲近的人因感染冠状病毒而住院或去世，持这一看法的人都占多数，且比例相近。此外，略多于半数的拉丁裔（54%）表示，他们预计一年后个人财务状况会有所改善；自疫情开始以来家庭经历过失业或工资损失的人与未经历过这些情况的人之间，仅存在不大的差异。
术语
本报告中，西班牙裔与拉丁裔两个术语可互换使用。
除非另有说明，“美国出生”一词指生来即为美国公民的人，包括出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土的人，以及出生于其他地方但父母中至少一方为美国公民的人。
除非另有说明，“外国出生”一词指出生于美国境外且父母双方均非美国公民的人。本报告中，“外国出生”与“移民”两个术语可互换使用。
第二代指出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土，且父母中至少一方为第一代移民的人。
第三代或更高世代指出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土，且父母双方均出生于美国50个州、哥伦比亚特区、波多黎各或其他美国领土的人。

在疫情期间，拉丁裔对国家变得更加乐观。约一半（49%）表示，他们对国家的发展方向感到满意，高于2020年六月的20%。这是自2012年以来拉丁裔对国家发展方向最满意的一次，当时有51%的人表示满意。与此同时，认为全国已经度过疫情最严重阶段的人所占比例大幅上升，从2020年四月的23%升至2021年三月的65%。此外，与疫情前相比，如今拉丁裔成年人更有可能表示，美国拉丁裔的处境在过去一年有所改善或基本保持不变，而表示拉丁裔处境恶化的可能性则有所降低。

query:
In the survey, what is the exact number of Latinos who report They expect their financial
situation as well as their family’s
to be better a year from now and belong to the group Live in a household with
job or wage loss during
the pandemic? Round the answer down to the nearest integer.

paragraphs.text: More than a year into the pandemic, Latinos in the United States say COVID19 has harmed them and their loved ones in many ways. About half say a family member or close friend has been hospitalized or died from the coronavirus, and a similar share say they or someone in their household has lost a job or taken a pay cut during the pandemic. Yet amid these hardships, Latinos are upbeat about the future. Nearly twothirds say the worst of the coronavirus outbreak is behind the country, and a majority say they expect their financial situation and that of their family to improve over the next year.

Job and wage losses in Latino households during the pandemic were just as likely for those born in another country as those born in the U.S., according to a bilingual, online survey of 3,375 U.S. Latino adults conducted in March 2021. However, among immigrant Latinos, some groups were harder hit than others – a relatively high share (58%) of Latino immigrants without U.S. citizenship and without a green card say they or someone in their household has lost a job or wages since February 2020, compared with 45% of naturalized U.S. citizen immigrants who say this.1

Yet Latinos see better days ahead for themselves and the country, even if they have experienced hardship due to COVID-19. Most Latinos say they think the worst of the problems the country is facing from the outbreak are behind us, with similar majorities saying so among those who have had and not had someone close to them hospitalized or die due to the coronavirus. In addition, a slight majority of Latinos (54%) say they expect their personal financial situation will be better a year from now, with only modest differences between those in households that have and have not experienced a loss of jobs or wages since the start of the pandemic.
Terminology
The terms Hispanic and Latino are used interchangeably in this report.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term U.S. born refers to people who are U.S. citizens at birth, including people born in the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories, as well as those born elsewhere to at least one parent who is a U.S. citizen.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term foreign born refers to persons born outside of the United States to parents neither of whom was a U.S. citizen. The terms foreign born and immigrant are used interchangeably in this report.
Second generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with at least one first-generation, or immigrant, parent.

Third or higher generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with both parents born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories.

Over the course of the pandemic, Latinos have become more optimistic about the country. About half (49%) say they are satisfied with the nation’s direction, up from June 2020, when 20% said the same. This is the most satisfied Latinos have been with the nation’s direction since 2012, when 51% said so. At the same time, the share saying the worst of the pandemic is behind us as a nation is up sharply, from 23% in April 2020 to 65% in March 2021. Meanwhile, Latino adults are more likely today than before the pandemic to say the situation of U.S. Latinos has improved or stayed about the same over the past year, and they are less likely to say the situation of Latinos has worsened.

query:
Nell’indagine, qual è il numero esatto di latinoamericani che dichiarano «Si aspettano che la propria situazione
finanziaria e quella della loro famiglia
migliorino tra un anno» e appartengono al gruppo «Vivono in un nucleo familiare con
perdite di lavoro o riduzioni dello stipendio durante
la pandemia»? Arrotonda la risposta per difetto all’intero più vicino.

paragraphs.text: A più di un anno dall'inizio della pandemia, i latinoamericani negli Stati Uniti affermano che il COVID19 ha danneggiato loro e i loro cari in molti modi. Circa la metà afferma che un familiare o un amico stretto è stato ricoverato in ospedale o è morto a causa del coronavirus, e una quota simile afferma che loro stessi o qualcuno nel loro nucleo familiare ha perso il lavoro o subito una riduzione della retribuzione durante la pandemia. Eppure, nonostante queste difficoltà, i latinoamericani sono ottimisti sul futuro. Quasi due terzi affermano che il paese si è lasciato alle spalle il peggio dell'epidemia di coronavirus, e la maggioranza afferma di aspettarsi un miglioramento della propria situazione finanziaria e di quella della propria famiglia nel corso del prossimo anno.

Le perdite di posti di lavoro e le riduzioni delle retribuzioni nei nuclei familiari latinoamericani durante la pandemia erano altrettanto probabili per le persone nate in un altro paese quanto per quelle nate negli Stati Uniti, secondo un sondaggio online bilingue condotto su 3,375 adulti latinoamericani negli Stati Uniti nel marzo 2021. Tuttavia, tra gli immigrati latinoamericani, alcuni gruppi sono stati colpiti più duramente di altri: una quota relativamente elevata (58%) di immigrati latinoamericani senza cittadinanza statunitense e senza carta verde afferma che loro stessi o qualcuno nel loro nucleo familiare ha perso il lavoro o subito una riduzione della retribuzione dal febbraio 2020, rispetto a 45% degli immigrati naturalizzati cittadini statunitensi che affermano la stessa cosa.1

Eppure i latinoamericani intravedono giorni migliori per sé e per il paese, anche se hanno vissuto difficoltà dovute al COVID-19. La maggior parte dei latinoamericani afferma di ritenere che il peggio dei problemi che il paese sta affrontando a causa dell'epidemia sia ormai alle spalle, con maggioranze simili che esprimono questa opinione sia tra coloro che hanno avuto una persona cara ricoverata o deceduta a causa del coronavirus sia tra coloro che non l'hanno avuta. Inoltre, una lieve maggioranza dei latinoamericani (54%) afferma di aspettarsi che la propria situazione finanziaria personale sarà migliore tra un anno, con differenze soltanto modeste tra coloro che appartengono a nuclei familiari che hanno subito perdite di posti di lavoro o riduzioni delle retribuzioni dall'inizio della pandemia e coloro che non le hanno subite.
Terminologia
I termini ispanico e latinoamericano sono usati in modo intercambiabile in questo rapporto.

Salvo diversa indicazione, il termine nati negli Stati Uniti si riferisce alle persone che sono cittadine statunitensi dalla nascita, comprese quelle nate nei 50 stati degli Stati Uniti, nel Distretto di Columbia, a Porto Rico o in altri territori statunitensi, nonché quelle nate altrove da almeno un genitore cittadino statunitense.

Salvo diversa indicazione, il termine nati all'estero si riferisce alle persone nate al di fuori degli Stati Uniti da genitori nessuno dei quali era cittadino statunitense. I termini nati all'estero e immigrati sono usati in modo intercambiabile in questo rapporto.
La seconda generazione comprende le persone nate nei 50 stati, nel Distretto di Columbia, a Porto Rico o in altri territori statunitensi con almeno un genitore di prima generazione, ossia immigrato.

La terza generazione o le generazioni successive comprendono le persone nate nei 50 stati, nel Distretto di Columbia, a Porto Rico o in altri territori statunitensi con entrambi i genitori nati nei 50 stati, nel Distretto di Columbia, a Porto Rico o in altri territori statunitensi.

Nel corso della pandemia, i latinoamericani sono diventati più ottimisti riguardo al paese. Circa la metà (49%) afferma di essere soddisfatta della direzione in cui sta andando il paese, una quota in aumento rispetto al giugno 2020, quando 20% affermava lo stesso. Si tratta del livello di soddisfazione più alto dei latinoamericani riguardo alla direzione del paese dal 2012, quando 51% esprimeva questa opinione. Allo stesso tempo, la quota di coloro che affermano che, come nazione, ci siamo lasciati alle spalle il peggio della pandemia è aumentata nettamente, passando da 23% nell'aprile 2020 a 65% nel marzo 2021. Nel frattempo, gli adulti latinoamericani sono oggi più propensi rispetto a prima della pandemia ad affermare che la situazione dei latinoamericani negli Stati Uniti è migliorata o è rimasta pressoché invariata nell'ultimo anno, e sono meno propensi ad affermare che la situazione dei latinoamericani è peggiorata.

situation as well as their family’s
to be better a year from now and belong to the group Live in a household with
job or wage loss during
the pandemic? Round the answer down to the nearest integer.

paragraphs.text: More than a year into the pandemic, Latinos in the United States say COVID19 has harmed them and their loved ones in many ways. About half say a family member or close friend has been hospitalized or died from the coronavirus, and a similar share say they or someone in their household has lost a job or taken a pay cut during the pandemic. Yet amid these hardships, Latinos are upbeat about the future. Nearly twothirds say the worst of the coronavirus outbreak is behind the country, and a majority say they expect their financial situation and that of their family to improve over the next year.

Job and wage losses in Latino households during the pandemic were just as likely for those born in another country as those born in the U.S., according to a bilingual, online survey of 3,375 U.S. Latino adults conducted in March 2021. However, among immigrant Latinos, some groups were harder hit than others – a relatively high share (58%) of Latino immigrants without U.S. citizenship and without a green card say they or someone in their household has lost a job or wages since February 2020, compared with 45% of naturalized U.S. citizen immigrants who say this.1

Yet Latinos see better days ahead for themselves and the country, even if they have experienced hardship due to COVID-19. Most Latinos say they think the worst of the problems the country is facing from the outbreak are behind us, with similar majorities saying so among those who have had and not had someone close to them hospitalized or die due to the coronavirus. In addition, a slight majority of Latinos (54%) say they expect their personal financial situation will be better a year from now, with only modest differences between those in households that have and have not experienced a loss of jobs or wages since the start of the pandemic.
Terminology
The terms Hispanic and Latino are used interchangeably in this report.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term U.S. born refers to people who are U.S. citizens at birth, including people born in the 50 U.S. states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories, as well as those born elsewhere to at least one parent who is a U.S. citizen.

Unless otherwise indicated, the term foreign born refers to persons born outside of the United States to parents neither of whom was a U.S. citizen. The terms foreign born and immigrant are used interchangeably in this report.
Second generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with at least one first-generation, or immigrant, parent.

Third or higher generation refers to people born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories with both parents born in the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or other U.S. territories.

Over the course of the pandemic, Latinos have become more optimistic about the country. About half (49%) say they are satisfied with the nation’s direction, up from June 2020, when 20% said the same. This is the most satisfied Latinos have been with the nation’s direction since 2012, when 51% said so. At the same time, the share saying the worst of the pandemic is behind us as a nation is up sharply, from 23% in April 2020 to 65% in March 2021. Meanwhile, Latino adults are more likely today than before the pandemic to say the situation of U.S. Latinos has improved or stayed about the same over the past year, and they are less likely to say the situation of Latinos has worsened.

query:
Wat is in de enquête het exacte aantal Latino’s dat ‘Verwachten dat hun eigen financiële
situatie en die van hun gezin
over een jaar beter zullen zijn’ aangeeft en tot de groep ‘Wonen in een huishouden met
baanverlies of loonverlaging tijdens
de pandemie’ behoort? Rond het antwoord naar beneden af op een geheel getal.

paragraphs.text: Meer dan een jaar na het begin van de pandemie zeggen Latino’s in de Verenigde Staten dat COVID19 hen en hun dierbaren op veel manieren heeft geschaad. Ongeveer de helft zegt dat een familielid of goede vriend vanwege het coronavirus in het ziekenhuis is opgenomen of eraan is overleden, en een vergelijkbaar aandeel zegt dat zijzelf of iemand in hun huishouden tijdens de pandemie een baan heeft verloren of loon heeft moeten inleveren. Toch zijn Latino’s ondanks deze moeilijkheden optimistisch over de toekomst. Bijna twee derde zegt dat het ergste van de uitbraak van het coronavirus voor het land achter de rug is, en een meerderheid zegt te verwachten dat hun financiële situatie en die van hun gezin het komende jaar zullen verbeteren.

Volgens een tweetalige online-enquête onder 3,375 volwassen Latino’s in de VS, uitgevoerd in maart 2021, kwamen baan- en loonverlies tijdens de pandemie in Latino-huishoudens even vaak voor bij mensen die in een ander land zijn geboren als bij mensen die in de VS zijn geboren. Onder geïmmigreerde Latino’s werden sommige groepen echter harder getroffen dan andere: een relatief groot aandeel (58%) van de Latino-immigranten zonder Amerikaans staatsburgerschap en zonder green card zegt dat zijzelf of iemand in hun huishouden sinds februari 2020 een baan of loon heeft verloren, tegenover 45% van de immigranten die tot Amerikaans staatsburger zijn genaturaliseerd.1

Toch zien Latino’s betere tijden tegemoet voor zichzelf en het land, ook als zij door COVID-19 moeilijkheden hebben ondervonden. De meeste Latino’s zeggen te denken dat de ergste problemen waarmee het land door de uitbraak wordt geconfronteerd achter ons liggen. Vergelijkbare meerderheden zeggen dit onder zowel degenen die wel als degenen die niet hebben meegemaakt dat iemand in hun naaste omgeving vanwege het coronavirus in het ziekenhuis is opgenomen of eraan is overleden. Daarnaast zegt een kleine meerderheid van de Latino’s (54%) te verwachten dat hun persoonlijke financiële situatie over een jaar beter zal zijn, met slechts geringe verschillen tussen mensen in huishoudens die sinds het begin van de pandemie wel en geen baan- of loonverlies hebben meegemaakt.
Terminologie
De termen Hispanic en Latino worden in dit rapport door elkaar gebruikt.

Tenzij anders aangegeven, verwijst de term in de VS geboren naar mensen die bij hun geboorte Amerikaans staatsburger zijn, met inbegrip van mensen die zijn geboren in de 50 Amerikaanse staten, het District of Columbia, Puerto Rico of andere Amerikaanse territoria, evenals mensen die elders zijn geboren met ten minste één ouder die Amerikaans staatsburger is.

Tenzij anders aangegeven, verwijst de term in het buitenland geboren naar personen die buiten de Verenigde Staten zijn geboren uit ouders die geen van beiden Amerikaans staatsburger waren. De termen in het buitenland geboren en immigrant worden in dit rapport door elkaar gebruikt.

Tweede generatie verwijst naar mensen die zijn geboren in de 50 staten, het District of Columbia, Puerto Rico of andere Amerikaanse territoria en van wie ten minste één ouder tot de eerste generatie behoort, oftewel immigrant is.

Derde of latere generatie verwijst naar mensen die zijn geboren in de 50 staten, het District of Columbia, Puerto Rico of andere Amerikaanse territoria en van wie beide ouders zijn geboren in de 50 staten, het District of Columbia, Puerto Rico of andere Amerikaanse territoria.

In de loop van de pandemie zijn Latino’s optimistischer geworden over het land. Ongeveer de helft (49%) zegt tevreden te zijn met de richting die het land opgaat, een stijging ten opzichte van juni 2020, toen 20% hetzelfde zei. Latino’s zijn niet meer zo tevreden geweest met de richting die het land opgaat sinds 2012, toen 51% dat zei. Tegelijkertijd is het aandeel dat zegt dat het ergste van de pandemie voor ons als land achter de rug is sterk gestegen, van 23% in april 2020 naar 65% in maart 2021. Intussen zeggen volwassen Latino’s tegenwoordig vaker dan vóór de pandemie dat de situatie van Latino’s in de VS het afgelopen jaar is verbeterd of ongeveer gelijk is gebleven, en zeggen ze minder vaak dat de situatie van Latino’s is verslechterd.
